items.body:
## Motivation

DMD2 distillation in miles-diffusion (radixark/miles_diffusion#333) scores the student's samples with the teacher under CFG, inside the trainer. The trainer has no text encoders, so it replays the cond that the rollout returns in `denoising_env`. The student samples unguided (guidance 1), and then the engine never encodes the negative prompt: `neg_cond_kwargs` comes back empty and the teacher can't run CFG.

## Modifications

- `RolloutRequest` / `SamplingParams`: new `rollout_return_neg_cond_kwargs`, default `False` (no behavior change).

## Motivation

Fixes #45512. `FanOutCommunicator.queueing_call` awaited the all-rank reply

dispatch until the active call finished.

items.title: [ROCm] Bump UCX to v1.23.0-rc1 so NIXL uses rocm_ipc
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Bumps UCX to v1.23.0-rc1 on ROCm to restore NIXL's rocm_ipc GPU-to-GPU transport, fixing a regression that fell back to TCP/host staging and caused hangs under long-context loads.

items.title: [Perf] muse_spark: Run the one-token router GEMV on CuTe DSL
items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: computes FP32 router logits on a side stream in every MoE layer, and the MoE waits for it. At one decode token cuBLAS runs this as a split-K GEMV plus a separate reduce kernel.
items.body:
## Motivation

`MuseSpark1xRouter` computes FP32 router logits on a side stream in every MoE layer, and the MoE waits for it. At one decode token cuBLAS runs this as a split-K GEMV plus a separate reduce kernel. In NVFP4 batch-1 decode on GB300 the main stream waits 146-152 us per step (of about 5.4 ms) for the router.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/gemm/muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` (new): a CuTe DSL FP32 GEMV with one launch, no split-K workspace and a fixed reduction order, so results are deterministic and differ from cuBLAS only by FP32 summation order
- `router_gemv_cute_eligible`

items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Replay one row for prefill chunks far from the prompt end
items.author: ischencheng
items.summary: With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end.
items.body:
## Overview

With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end. A 124K prompt in 16K chunks now skips 7 of its 8 replay tails. The same idea is DeepSeek DeepInfer's `clip_prefix` rule.

Related: #61682 does this on ROCm with one row for every unfinished chunk. That rule lets a later step read replay-layer KV that no step wrote (inline comment there). This PR covers CUDA and keeps that case closed

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Fall back to transparent hugepages when none are reserved
items.author: Lzy17
items.summary: When is set but no huge pages are reserved, now falls back to transparent huge pages (THP) before falling back to 4 KiB pages. THP needs no reservation and no root.
items.body:
## What
When `SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE` is set but no huge pages are reserved (`nr_hugepages=0`), `alloc_mmap` now falls back to transparent huge pages (THP) before falling back to 4 KiB pages. THP needs no reservation and no root.

## Why
The host pool is then registered with the NIC. Some NICs cap one registration at about 1M page-table entries (about 4 GiB of 4 KiB pages), so a large host pool on 4 KiB pages fails with `ibv_reg_mr` EINVAL/ENOMEM. 2 MiB pages cut the entry count by 512x. Reserving huge pages needs root, which shared CI nodes do not give.

items.title: [Feat] srt: Balance uvicorn tokenizer workers with per-worker SO_REUSEPORT listeners
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds optional SO_REUSEPORT so each uvicorn tokenizer worker binds its own listener, preventing burst imbalance on Linux's shared accept queue.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--tokenizer-worker-num N` the HTTP server runs N uvicorn workers that all accept from one shared listening socket. Linux does not round-robin a shared accept queue: whichever workers wake first take the connections, so a burst can land mostly on one worker. A long-lived connection (a streaming response, a WebSocket session) then stays on that worker for its whole life, so the imbalance persists and the busy worker's event loop adds latency to every request it holds.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/serving.py`: new opt-in `--enable-http-worker-reus

items.title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2] Use int64 logits row offsets in the grammar bitmask kernel
items.author: cycancode
items.summary: Fixes integer overflow in MRV2 grammar bitmask kernel where int32 row offsets exceed 2^31, causing out-of-bounds writes during large-batch structured-output spec decoding.
items.body:
## Overview

The MRV2 grammar bitmask kernel computes the logits row offset as an int32 product, so it overflows once `row * vocab_size` exceeds 2**31. With a 151936-token vocab that happens from logits row 14135, which wide spec-decode verification with structured outputs can reach at large batch sizes (e.g. 15 draft tokens and ~900 requests). The kernel then writes `-inf` outside the logits tensor and leaves the intended row unmasked. This loads the row index as int64, like the other MRV2 row-offset kernels fixed in #46560 and for #57030.

## Claims

- Grammar bitmasks are applied to the rig

items.author: shijie-lyu
items.summary: Fixes GPT-OSS chat tokenization mismatch by routing /tokenize through Harmony's render_chat so it matches the chat completion render endpoint.
items.body:
## Overview

For GPT-OSS, `/tokenize` renders a chat with the model's HF chat template, while the chat route renders it with Harmony. So `/tokenize` returns ids that the chat route never prefills, which breaks the invariant `test_tokenize_matches_render_for_multimodal_input` already states for multimodal input: `/tokenize` matches `/v1/chat/completions/render`. This PR renders GPT-OSS chats in `/tokenize` through `OnlineRenderer.render_chat`, the function the chat route and the render endpoint use.

## Claims

- For GPT-OSS chats, `/tokenize` returns the ids of `/v1/chat/completions/render`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix out-of-bounds block-table read in Triton unified attention
items.author: vadiklyutiy
items.summary: Fixes an out-of-bounds block-table read in Triton unified attention and INT4 per-token-head kernels by masking loads beyond sequence boundaries, with regression tests.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61803. Sometimes the KV tile is wider than the KV block, for example the 32-wide prefill tile with block size 16. Then `kernel_unified_attention` reads block-table entries past the end of the sequence's row. compute-sanitizer reports invalid global reads at the unmasked block-table `tl.load`, and the launch fails. This PR masks that load with `tile_mask`, which every other load in the loop already uses. It makes the same change in the INT4 per-token-head kernel `_attn_packed`, which has a copy of the loop behind the same `unified_attention` entry point.

Compared with #6181

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix out-of-bounds write of non-inplace final_state in fused recurrent delta-rule kernels
items.author: vadiklyutiy
items.summary: Fixes out-of-bounds GPU memory write in fused recurrent delta-rule kernels by allocating B*T rows instead of T for final_state when batch size exceeds one.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61800. The bug shows with `inplace_final_state=False` and a dense `[B, T]` batch where `B > 1`. In that case, `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` allocates `final_state` with `T` rows, but the kernel writes one row per token of the whole batch. So every sequence after the first writes past the end of the buffer. This PR allocates `B * T` rows. It makes the same change in the six other wrappers that allocate the same buffer for the same kernel store.

Compared with #61808, this fix:

- Also repairs the six other wrappers that have the same short buffer: `fused_recurrent_kda`

items.title: [Fix] constrained: Do not cache grammar poll timeouts as invalid grammars
items.author: shijie-lyu
items.summary: When a grammar request waits past, caches for that key. treats any cached object as a hit, so every later request with the same schema is aborted with until (which needs an idle server) or a restart.
items.body:
## Motivation

When a grammar request waits past `SGLANG_GRAMMAR_MAX_POLL_ITERATIONS`, `GrammarManager.get_ready_grammar_requests` caches `InvalidGrammarObject("Grammar preprocessing timed out")` for that key. `BaseGrammarBackend.get_cached_or_future_value` treats any cached object as a hit, so every later request with the same schema is aborted with `Failed to compile json grammar: Grammar preprocessing timed out` until `/flush_cache` (which needs an idle server) or a restart.

A timeout is not a property of the schema: the poll counter also runs while the compile waits in the shared executor

Batch-invariant (BI) inference with MXFP8 routed experts does work proportional to `max_tokens` on every decode step, whatever the number of live tokens. items.title: [Perf] moe: Reduce temporary memory in Muse Marlin and W4A8 scaling
items.author: ch-wan
items.summary: Restore Muse Marlin's projection workspace budget from before #44994 and remove the full activation copy used by W4A8 dynamic scaling, while keeping padded and nonlocal routes safe.
items.body:
## Motivation

Restore Muse Marlin's projection workspace budget from before #44994 and remove the full activation copy used by W4A8 dynamic scaling, while keeping padded and nonlocal routes safe.

## Changes

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Refactors the Rust radix-tree cache system from an enum-based CacheAction model to a trait-based per-action struct implementation for better maintainability.
items.body:
Stacked on #45439 (`oss-sync-f2543fd394`): this pull request is based on that branch and its own diff is only its top commit. Please read it after #45439; once that lands this branch is rebased onto `main`.

## Motivation

items.title: [Perf] cookbook: enable custom all-reduce for GB300 BF16 Muse Spark
items.author: Waterpine
items.summary: On GB300, the BF16 Muse Spark checkpoint runs TP8 across two nodes of one NVL72 rack. Custom all-reduce v2 supports a multi-node group when all ranks share one NVLink clique, but only if PyTorch's caching allocator is VMM-backed.
items.body:
## Motivation

On GB300, the BF16 Muse Spark checkpoint runs TP8 across two nodes of one NVL72 rack. Custom all-reduce v2 supports a multi-node group when all ranks share one NVLink clique, but only if PyTorch's caching allocator is VMM-backed (`custom_all_reduce_v2.py`). The cookbook recipe does not enable that, so the server logs "CustomAllreduce is disabled because this process group spans across nodes" and every decode all-reduce goes through NCCL. At batch size 1 that is 4.4 ms of a 10.0 ms decode step.

Depends on [#45422](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45422): the GB300 BF16

items.title: [None][perf] MiniMax-M3: BF16-split tensor-core router GEMM
items.author: pranav-nvidia
items.summary: Splits MiniMax-M3 FP32 router GEMM into three BF16 terms to enable tensor-core compute, achieving 1.3-2.1x speedup while preserving FP32-grade numerical accuracy.
items.body:
## Description

`MiniMaxM3Gate` computes its router logits in FP32 with `F.linear(hidden_states.float(), weight)`. That has two costs. `F.linear` follows torch's FP32 matmul precision, which the NGC PyTorch containers set to TF32 through `TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1`; at TF32 the logits move enough to flip near-tied top-4 expert choices against the FP32 reference (SGLang routes this model in FP32). And a true FP32 GEMM cannot use tensor cores, so this small per-layer op runs as a SIMT SGEMM.

This change keeps FP32-grade routing on tensor cores:

- `load_weights` splits the FP32 router

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] DSpark: Enable the simulated-acceptance fast paths on CUDA
items.author: YAMY1234
items.summary: Removes HIP-only gates from DSpark's simulated-acceptance fast paths (verify skip, fold, greedy), enabling CUDA to achieve ~25% throughput improvement without affecting real serving.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set (simulated acceptance for benchmarking), DSpark already has three fast paths, but they are gated to HIP:

- the verify skips the draft / target accept sampling (softmax + rejection), whose result the simulated length overwrites;
- the accept and the sampled bonus fold into the verify CUDA graph (`SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`);
- temperature-only rows are treated as greedy (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY`).

On CUDA the same simulated runs still pay for the discarded sampling and the unfolded accept. This PR lets CUDA take the same paths.

items.title: [RFC] pd: Prefill short requests on the decode worker that caches their prefix (PPD)
items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: So turn N+1 misses on prefill at the first output token, while the decode worker's radix cache holds prompt N plus output N. With HiCache, cache hit rates of 90%+ are common for agentic sessions, so the computed part is often a few hundred tokens, and the fixe…
items.body:
## TL;DR

In agentic and multi-turn traffic, the decode worker that served the previous turn already holds almost all of the next prompt in its radix cache: the previous prompt plus the tokens it decoded. Today the next turn still goes prefill -> KV transfer -> decode, even when only a few hundred tokens are new. This RFC lets the router send such a request **only to the decode worker**, which prefills the uncached suffix itself (chunked prefill), then decodes it. We call this **PPD** (prefill on the decode worker, for short prefills). Requests the router does not mark keep the normal PD path,

items.author: IvanShan177
items.summary: merges the prefix splits with weights. A split whose KV range is empty skips the stage1 store of and only writes the lse sentinel, so its weight is 0.

## Motivation

`_verify_combine_stage2` merges the prefix splits with weights `exp(lse - max)`. A split whose KV range is empty skips the stage1 store of `Att_Out` and only writes the `-inf` lse sentinel, so its weight is 0. Stage2 still loads that split's `Att_Out` row, which holds whatever the reused scratch buffer (`VerifySplitKV.att_out`, cached per shape in `_VK_CACHE`) last contained, and computes `ao * 0`. If that stale memory is nan or inf, `0 * nan = nan` and the whole draft row of the output becomes nan.

items.summary: Fixes sgl-router CI reruns by reading the `run-ci` label live instead of from a frozen payload, so `/tag-and-rerun-ci` properly triggers tier jobs.
items.body:
## Motivation

`/tag-and-rerun-ci` never starts the sgl-router CI tiers. Seen on #45103 (and #42818 before it): the PR ends up with the `run-ci` label, the "PR Test (sgl-router)" check is green, and every tier job is `skipped`.

Three things in `pr-test-sgl-router.yml` combine to cause it:

1. The gate reads `github.event.pull_request.labels`, a payload frozen when the run was triggered. A rerun replays that payload, so a rerun after the label was added skips again.
2. The slash handler adds `run-ci` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub fires no `labeled` event for such label changes, so no new run
discussion: /tag-and-rerun-ci

items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.title: [Fix] mamba: End the prefill chunk at the Mamba branching point
items.author: AMD-yanfeiwang
items.summary: With, a prefill extend snapshots the recurrent state at one position. Normally that is the last checkpoint-grid boundary of the prompt.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer`, a prefill extend snapshots the recurrent state at one position. Normally that is the last checkpoint-grid boundary of the prompt. When the Full-KV match runs past the matched Mamba state, `match_prefix` reports a branching point. If that point lies inside the extend, the one snapshot is moved there, and the prompt end gets no state. items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pad Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram inputs for piecewise CUDA graph replays
items.author: vllmellm
items.summary: Fixes stale n-gram buffer reads during piecewise CUDA graph replays on ROCm by padding Qwen4Exp PLE inputs, eliminating history-dependent incorrect outputs.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61486

The Qwen4Exp AMD backend computes PLE n-gram ids inside PIECEWISE CUDA graph pieces, where the request search keeps the count the piece was captured with, but `Qwen4ExpModelState` only refreshed the live batch's rows of `query_start_loc` and
`ngram_context`. Replays read a stale tail, hashed the wrong n-gram and made the answer depend on what the server had served before. This pads both buffers.

## Claims

- PLE n-gram inputs no longer depend on server history: 0/300 short prompts change their answer after a 16-way burst, versus 77/300 before.
- Bit-identical replay

items.body:
## Description

**Problem.** In each MiniMax-M3 decode step, the index scorer picks the 16 KV blocks every query attends to. To do that, it reads the whole index-K cache: one 128-dim FP8 key per cached token, in each of the 57 sparse layers. Every TP rank reads all of index-K to score only its own index heads, so the same bytes are read TP times. At 131k-token contexts this read dominates the scorer: about 70 µs per layer at TP2, batch 24.

**What this PR does** (`sparse_attention_config.index_tp_split`, off by default):
- **Split the read.** Rank r reads rows r, r + TP, ... of every 128-token

`MultiConnector` never forwarded `get_kv_connector_kv_cache_events()` to its sub-connectors. This PR implements the method, aggregates events per sub-connector across workers, and routes each sub-connector its own events on the scheduler side.

items.author: eyeooo
items.summary: With and, every tokenizer worker writes with its own hourly. Their rotations race: a colliding rename overwrites the freshly rotated file, and the workers still holding it keep writing into an unlinked inode, so their logs are silently lost.

Fixes #45342. With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` and `--log-requests-target <dir>`, every tokenizer worker writes `<hostname>_0.log` with its own hourly `TimedRotatingFileHandler`. Without a collision, N-1 workers never rotate. The race window is much wider on network file systems.

## Motivation

BF16 projection output can round distinct token scores into a tie before the existing FP32 sampler-buffer cast. Inkling should be able to preserve FP32 projection output while retaining BF16 hidden states and head weights, without enabling the generic `--enable-fp32-lm-head` policy.

```python
# Preserve BF16 operands; produce FP32 projection output directly.
logits = torch.mm(hidden_bf16, weight_bf16.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)
```

Final sampler logits are already FP32 in either mode. Casting a rounded BF16 projection afterward cannot recover its lost score ordering.

items.title: [Fix] [NPU] Correct ModelSlim W4A8 MoE scale-bias TP sharding
items.author: JinyanYi
items.summary: ModelSlim integer W4A8 MoE loads the W2 matrix as a TP-local K shard, but currently allocates and loads all 16 checkpoint columns on every TP rank. The post-load reduction therefore applies a full-K quantization compensation to a partial-K matrix product.
items.body:
## Motivation

ModelSlim integer W4A8 MoE loads the W2 matrix as a TP-local K shard, but currently allocates and loads all 16 checkpoint `scale_bias` columns on every TP rank. items.title: [Doc] forward-hooks: Say that hooks don't run under CUDA graphs
items.author: aramasethu
items.summary: The forward hooks page says hooks are attached in and "run on every forward pass". That's not what happens.
items.body:
Fixes #45317

## Motivation

The forward hooks page says hooks are attached in `ModelRunner.initialize` and "run on every forward pass". That's not what happens. Hooks are registered **after** CUDA graph capture (`finalize_cuda_graph_capture`), and CUDA graph replay never runs Python hooks. With default settings on CUDA, decode and prefill both use CUDA graphs, so a hook can silently never run.

In #45317, a hook on `model.layers.14` of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (v0.5.21, NVIDIA L4) ran **0 times** for a 128-token request with default settings. It ran **128 times** with CUDA graphs disabled.

## Purpose

The ROCm BF16x3 router tier (`bf16x3_router_gemm_rocm`, fp32 gate weights as in MiniMax-M2/M3) only serves batches of 2048+ tokens. Decode batches above the gfx950 fp32 low-M kernel (M ≤ 32) and below 2048 fall back to `F.linear(x.float(), w)` on the fp32 pipe, which is both slower and less accurate.

This PR adds a split-K Triton kernel for that range:

items.author: luckyq
items.summary: Recurrent chunks and partial tails are described like attention chunks (hashes, tokens, parent,, ) with. Docstrings state that the residency is the state checkpoint at the last hash, not a reusable range.
items.body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` emits a `block_size=0` placeholder `BlockStored` for every group that has a load window. `MambaSpec` groups get a one-chunk window because they depend on a single state, not because their hashes are meaningless: the offloaded chunk is the recurrent state checkpoint at the chunk's last hash. External consumers that index offload residency (a KV-aware router with a CPU/KVCR tier) therefore cannot see where a hybrid prefix is reusable and overestimate it from the attention group (vllm-project/vllm#62510).

## Changes

- `events.py`: `describes_group()` return

## Overview

With `--use-fp64-gumbel`, Model Runner V2 still sends unseeded top-k/top-p batches to FlashInfer's fused sampler, which draws fp32 noise, so the flag is silently ignored for those steps. This skips the FlashInfer sampler when fp64 Gumbel is requested, matching the V1 sampler and MRV2's own XPU path.

- With `use_fp64_gumbel=True`, MRV2 samples unseeded top-k/top-p requests with fp64 Gumbel noise instead of FlashInfer.
- Without the flag, MRV2 keeps using the FlashInfer sampler as before.

items.author: chushic
items.summary: With MTP, GLM-5.2 runs the gfx950 DSA indexer logits kernel (, node 3 of the fused decode indexer) once per verify step on each of its 21 "full" indexer layers. Each request contributes 6 rows (the draft positions), and all 6 rows read the same KV pages, but l…
items.body:
## Motivation

With MTP, GLM-5.2 runs the gfx950 DSA indexer logits kernel (`logits_hist`, node 3 of the fused decode indexer) once per verify step on each of its 21 "full" indexer layers. Each request contributes 6 rows (the draft positions), and all 6 rows read the same KV pages, but `logits_hist_m` loads every page once per row. At small batches with long contexts the kernel is bound by those loads.

This PR reads each shared page once per slot of 3 rows, so a request reads each page twice instead of 6 times. The kernel gets up to 2.67x faster, and median interactivity on the InferenceX

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

items.title: [Perf][Sampler] Split the full-vocab passes of the Triton top-k/top-p kernel over several programs per row
items.author: kimseunghyun-kr
items.summary: With an active top-k, runs one program per row, and that program sweeps the whole vocab twice: once to gather outliers and once to apply the final mask. On A100 with a 248K vocab, one row takes about 360 µs of GPU time, and most of it is spent in those two swe…
items.body:
## Overview

With an active top-k, `_topk_topp_kernel` runs **one program per row**, and that program sweeps the whole vocab twice: once to gather outliers and once to apply the final mask. On A100 with a 248K vocab, one row takes about 360 µs of GPU time, and most of it is spent in those two sweeps. This PR splits the two sweeps over several programs per row. ## Description

**Problem.** In `_executor_loop_overlap`, forward(k) is launched before batch k-1 is processed (`_update_requests`, `_send_kv_async`, `_process_previous_batch`). `trtllm-llmapi-launch` stops the rank-0 MPI Comm Server (`mgmn_leader_node`) by running `mgmn_leader_node --action stop` right after its task exits. That stop client sends one shutdown request on a new connection and exits. The request can be lost, and then the job never ends.

**Why it is lost.** The server's control socket is a ZMQ PAIR socket, which talks to one peer at a time. items.author: Sunt-ing
items.summary: With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks.
items.body:

# What does this PR do?

With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks. For CP2 rank 0, length 64 caches positions `0…15, 48…63`, but length 32 needs `0…7, 24…31`. Taking a prefix of the old cache gives the wrong positions.

Rebuild the cache when a non-packed sequence shrinks with CP > 1. CP1 and packed inputs can still reuse the cache.

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

Add opt-in `SchedulePolicy(reduce_scatter_interval=k)` to MFSDP v2. A module reuses one full local-gradient buffer per trainable parameter group, accumulates in main-gradient precision, and reduces every `k` completed backwards. items.author: Sunt-ing
items.summary: With batch-invariant inference and MLA latent caching enabled, a new request entering prefill can change the generated log-probabilities of requests already decoding. Decode-only batches use absorbed MLA, while mixed batches use unabsorbed attention; switching…
items.body:

# What does this PR do?

With batch-invariant inference and MLA latent caching enabled, a new request entering prefill can change the generated log-probabilities of requests already decoding. Decode-only batches use absorbed MLA, while mixed batches use unabsorbed attention; switching between them changes floating-point evaluation order.

Use unabsorbed attention for both paths when `batch_invariant_mode=True`, as required by the [batch-invariant inference guarantee](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ce852bfb93f3

items.author: muditagrawal2007
items.summary: ran in the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that - loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and - overflows FP16 at temperature=0 (the divisor is floored to → → ).
items.body:
Fixes #7857.

## What

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` ran `last_token_logits.div_(temperature)` in
the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that

  - loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership
    at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and
  - overflows FP16 at temperature=0 (the divisor is floored to
    `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6` → `logits * 1e6` → `inf`).

Issue #7857 documents both failures on a trained Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K through
the dynamic engine: BF16 rounding changes which token wins at temperature=0.1,
top_p=0.9; FP16 scaling overflows at temperature=0.

`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

```python
PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

### What does this PR do?

Fix checkpoint saving in SFT and RL training using the Megatron engine with standard DDP, distributed optimization, and parameter-gather overlap enabled (DP > 1).

After an optimizer step, the updated weights are normally synchronized before the next forward pass. If training saves a checkpoint before that synchronization—for example, at a periodic checkpoint or the end of training—the save can succeed while some model weights are still out of date. **Both native Megatron-Core (MCore) checkpoints and Hugging Face-format exports can be affected**, because both backend

veRL pins Transformers 5.12.1, which has a slow CPU check for image/video special tokens. Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost **even when they contain only text**.

items.title: [MoE] Opt-in EP-size-invariant expert combine (fixed fp32 reduction tree)
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout.
items.body:
**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688) in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix cached Qwen3.5 forwards with Transformers 5, where convolution and recurrent state are stored in layer-scoped `DynamicCache` entries. The existing code accesses legacy top-level arrays and raises:

```text
AttributeError: 'DynamicCache' object has no attribute 'conv_states'
```

The patch reads and updates both legacy and layer-scoped cache state, including tensor-valued and state-indexed entries. Multi-token continuation retains the previous convolution context and recurrent state; single-token decoding uses the recurrent update path.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.body:
Replace MFSDP v2's `IndexedOrder` with `ExecutionOrder` so repeated calls to one module can have different prefetch successors. For example, in `A → B → A → C`, the two occurrences of `A` lead to `B` and `C` respectively.

As items are appended, a weak lookup records each unique module's index or marks it as repeated. Unique modules select their position by identity, preserving construction-order behavior for grouped VPP chunk calls. Repeated modules must match the next occurrence at the cursor; a mismatch raises without consuming it. `next_item(offset)` looks ahead without advancing execution

items.title: Fix FP8/FP4 context loss during GDN and KDA recompute
items.author: QiZhangNV
items.summary: When selective recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward.
items.body:
When selective `gdn` recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward. With MXFP8 parameter gathering enabled, this can also cause a missing `main_grad` error.

Use `te_checkpoint` for FP8/FP4 in GDN and KDA to preserve the quantization context, keeping the existing checkpoint path for non-quantized configurations.

Validated with 12 GPU regression cases and a single-node, four-GPU Qwen-style proxy covering MXFP8, NVFP4, and MXFP8 parameter gathering.

### What does this PR do?

Fix `fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu` when `param_offload=True` in the fully async trainer.

Slop free TLDR:

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。


## 工作原理

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

**工作流步骤：**

1. **检出（Checkout）** Fork 私有仓库的 `main` 分支（包含 `translate_md.py`、`skill.md`、`.po` 缓存）。
2. **同步（Sync）** Fork 的 `main` 分支与最新的上游 `main` 分支（通过 `git merge`），然后将同步后的 `main` 分支推送回 Fork。

### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. A `BaseTool` therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although `BaseTool.create` is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and `docs/sglang_multiturn/multiturn.rst` points to `BaseTool` for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.

This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

items.author: annika-modal
items.summary: VLM wrappers like delegate to an inner that owns the LM head. The critic's was assigned to the wrapper, so it was never called: the critic returned vocab-sized logits and the first value step failed the assertion in.

items.author: sdc17
items.summary: Nothing errors out and the loss still goes down, so it is easy to miss, but every CP > 1 run that goes through this code path has been training on wrong gradients since #1748. How wrong: - real layer (fla kernels, bf16), CP=4: the input gradient is off by 9.4%…

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

- all actor ranks loaded the same rollout

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix(rm_hub): stop substring-matching gpqa letter labels and short answers
items.author: shaurya416
items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: tengeel

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

## Summary

When `--use-kl-loss` is enabled with `kl_loss_coef == 0`, slime still
constructs the reference KL autograd graph and adds the following term to the
actor loss:

policy loss and its gradients into NaN. Multiplying by a zero coefficient does
not make a non-finite KL value harmless, because `0 * NaN` is still `NaN`.

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.body:
## Summary

1.Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend.
This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated weight updates with vLLM's native /update_weights lifecycle.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.

items.body:
## Summary
Add \`examples/mem_agent\`, a vime port of [MemAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02259) for long-context QA with RL:
- **Multi-turn rollout**: chunk-wise memory update + final \`\\boxed{}\` answer (HotpotQA reward)
- **Training**: GRPO on Qwen3-4B via vLLM colocate (\`run-qwen3-4b-train.sh\`)
- **Evaluation**: RULER-HQA offline eval via vLLM serve (\`run-eval.sh\`, \`eval_ruler_hqa.py\`)
- **Data prep**: HuggingFace dataset \`BytedTsinghua-SIA/hotpotqa\` -> training JSONL + eval JSON download
Also updates \`examples/README.md\` with a directory entry.
